notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; 7-week-old female C57BL/6 mice, n=4/group, single ICV injection of 15.2 nmol (100 ug). readout_value is TBD because Figure 1B is a grouped bar chart in which the two day-7 peaks (group means of roughly 9 and 6.5 on the 0-15 tolerability axis) and the smaller day-14 to day-21 bars (roughly 1.5-2.5) could not be assigned to individual ASOs with confidence from the colour key. Late-ONSET CNS toxicity: signs appeared at least 3 days after a single central injection, persisted for 6 days or more and worsened over time. The authors emphasise this is distinct from acute toxicity - no acute neurotoxicity was seen with ASO1, ASO3 or ASO4, and the acute toxicity of ASO2 resolved completely within 1 day. Tolerability scoring system in Supplementary Table S2 covers consciousness, motor function (ataxia, strength) and appearance (posture, breathing, home-cage activity). No recovery/reversal phase was run: animals were killed at a scheduled time point or when they reached a humane endpoint, and signs were progressive up to that point, so reversibility is recorded as irreversible on the evidence available rather than demonstrated permanence.
